sourcedFrom: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page (2024 — revision "Revision F 02.26.2024" on the back page)
cleanIntro:
The LWRCI IC-9 is a 9mm pistol-caliber carbine with AR-style lower controls and a chamber-ring delayed-blowback action: annular grooves cut into the chamber walls let the fired case expand and grip, slowing the one-piece carrier's rearward travel. It feeds from Glock-manufactured magazines.

An AR owner will find the takedown familiar with two differences. The buffer and its spring come out of the buffer tube as part of the field strip — with the hammer cocked, a tool on the buffer retainer lets them spring free — and the carrier slides out of the tilted upper on its own weight without catching on the charging handle. LWRCI's routine maintenance follows every firing session; its detailed maintenance — the firing pin out of the carrier and the breech face scrubbed — comes every 1,000 rounds or weekly in the field.

steps.title: Muzzle safe — magazine out
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction and keep it there. Press the magazine release on either side of the lower and pull the magazine out of the well; a tug while holding the release makes sure it comes free.
steps.prose: With a magazine still seated, working the charging handle only chambers the next round.
steps.quote: While pointing the muzzle in a safe direction, remove the magazine (if present) by depressing the magazine release and pulling the magazine out.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing Your Weapon, printed p.12

steps.title: Hold the bolt catch down
steps.action: Press and hold the bottom half of either bolt catch lever. The controls are ambidextrous, so either side works.
steps.prose: Holding the lower half of the catch is what traps the carrier to the rear when you draw it back.
steps.quote: Press and hold the bottom half of either bolt catch lever.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing Your Weapon, printed p.12

steps.title: Charging handle all the way back
steps.action: With the other hand, grasp the charging handle, press its latches and pull the handle and carrier firmly all the way to the rear. Any chambered round ejects; the carrier is trapped by the bolt catch.
steps.prose: Short of the full stroke the bolt catch has nothing to hold, and the carrier runs home again.
steps.quote: grasp the charging handle, depress the latch(es) and firmly pull the charging handle and carrier all the way to the rear.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing Your Weapon, printed p.12

steps.title: Charging handle home and latched
steps.action: Push the charging handle forward until it latches closed. The carrier stays locked to the rear on the bolt catch.
steps.prose: A handle left unlatched can be knocked back during the inspection that follows.
steps.quote: Return the charging handle to the closed and latched position.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing Your Weapon, printed p.13

steps.title: LOOK into the chamber
steps.action: Roll the carbine counter-clockwise until you can see the bolt and chamber through the ejection port. See an empty chamber and a carrier locked to the rear. In poor light, check by feel.
steps.prose: No case flying out is not proof of an empty chamber — the look is the check.
steps.caution: Do not depend on the fact that no casing was ejected on clearing.
steps.quote: Visually check to make sure that the chamber is clear and that the bolt is locked to the rear.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 3.1 Clearing Your Weapon, printed p.13

steps.title: Clear it again before anything comes apart
steps.action: Repeat the clearing check more than once before any pin moves. Leave the hammer cocked — do not dry-fire it — because the buffer comes out later with the hammer cocked.
steps.prose: LWRCI opens its field strip with this step because disassembly and cleaning are where negligent discharges happen.
steps.quote: Clear the firearm several times. Most negligent discharges occur during disassembly and cleaning operations.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.20

steps.title: Rear takedown pin out to its stop
steps.action: From the left side, press in the rear takedown pin. From the right side, pull it to the right until it stops.
steps.prose: The pin is captive; it stops at its detent and does not come out of the lower.
steps.quote: From the left-hand side, press in the rear takedown pin.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.20

steps.title: Front pivot pin the same way
steps.action: Do the same for the front pivot pin: press it in from the left, pull it to the right until it stops.
steps.prose: Both pins go out to their stops before the receivers part.
steps.quote: Repeat step 2 for the front pivot pin.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.20

steps.title: Upper off the lower
steps.action: Separate the upper receiver from the lower receiver.
steps.prose: The lower now gets its buffer out; the carrier and charging handle are still in the upper.
steps.quote: Separate the upper and lower receivers
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.20

steps.title: Buffer retainer down — buffer springs free
steps.action: With the hammer still cocked, press the buffer retainer down with a screwdriver, punch or similar tool. The buffer springs out of the tube.
steps.prose: A cocked hammer is lying flat and clear of the buffer's path; a dropped hammer stands in the way.
steps.quote: With the hammer cocked, depress the buffer retainer using a screwdriver, punch, or other suitable tool. The buffer should spring free.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.21

steps.title: Buffer and spring out
steps.action: Pull the buffer and its spring out of the lower. If the spring catches on the buffer retainer, rotate it counter-clockwise until the buffer is far enough out to come free easily.
steps.prose: The spring is under some tension until it clears the tube; keep a hand on the buffer.
steps.quote: Pull on the buffer to remove the buffer and spring from the lower receiver.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.21

steps.title: Carrier out of the upper
steps.action: Tilt the back of the upper receiver down. The carrier assembly slides out under its own weight.
steps.prose: Unlike an AR-15 carrier group, the IC-9's carrier does not hang up on the charging handle — no need to pull the handle first.
steps.quote: Tilt the back of the upper receiver down. The carrier assembly will slide out from its own weight.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.21

steps.title: Charging handle back and down out
steps.action: Pull the charging handle fully to the rear, then move it downward so the tabs at its end pass through the cut-out in the charging handle slot.
steps.prose: The handle only comes out where its tabs meet the cut-out at the back of its travel.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle fully towards the rear.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.21

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: upper receiver with barrel, carrier assembly, charging handle, buffer and spring, and the lower receiver. DEEP CLEAN carries LWRCI's detailed disassembly — the stock off the buffer tube and the firing pin out of the carrier.
steps.prose: LWRCI's own limit: nothing beyond its field strip and detailed disassembly outside the factory or a gunsmith's shop.
steps.quote: Please note that rifles should not be broken down beyond the field strip unless in a controlled environment, such as the factory or in a gunsmith’s shop.
steps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 5.2 Field Stripping, printed p.20

deepSteps.title: Stock off the buffer tube
deepSteps.action: Grasp the adjustment lever on the underside of the stock and pull it straight down to disengage the stock pin, then slide the stock off the end of the buffer tube.
deepSteps.prose: Keep the lever pulled down until the stock is clear of the tube; the stock pin is what holds it in each position.
deepSteps.quote: Pull the adjustment lever straight down to disengage the stock pin, and then slide the stock off the end of the buffer tube.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.22

deepSteps.title: Firing pin out of the carrier
deepSteps.action: Pull out the firing pin retaining pin. The firing pin spring pushes the firing pin out of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: The pin comes out under spring pressure — point the carrier into your palm or a tray so neither part is lost.
deepSteps.quote: Remove firing pin from the carrier by pulling out the firing pin retaining pin. The firing pin will be pushed out by the firing pin spring.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.22

deepSteps.title: LWRCI's stopping point
deepSteps.action: Stop here. The book's detailed disassembly ends with the firing pin out; nothing else on the carrier or in the receivers comes apart for cleaning.
deepSteps.prose: LWRCI defines this level as everything that comes apart without specialized tools; anything further belongs to the factory or a gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: Detail disassembly is simply breaking down the rifle as much as possible without specialized tools.
deepSteps.cite: LWRCI IC-9 — Operator's Manual (Chamber Ring Delayed Blowback Operating System) — Revision F 02.26.2024 — printed on the back page — 5.3 Detailed Disassembly, printed p.22

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Solvent-soaked patch on a cleaning rod, pushed from the chamber end to the muzzle; let the barrel sit for several minutes.
Bore brush on the rod: punch the bore several times to break the build-up free.
Dry patches through the bore until they come out clean.

cleaning.name: CARRIER
tasks: Scrub the bolt face with a nylon brush dipped in solvent.
Deep clean: scrub the breech face with a nylon brush and solvent, paying particular attention to fouling in the extractor groove.
Wipe the solvent off thoroughly with a rag.
Moderate coat of lube on the carrier, especially the surfaces that face down — just visible to the eye, spread with a brush, cloth or finger.
The breech face does not need lubrication.
Do not use water-based lubricants such as WD-40 — LWRCI says the water content can aid corrosion.

cleaning.name: UPPER RECEIVER
tasks: Wipe the inside of the upper receiver with a cloth slightly dampened with solvent, then dry it.
Coat of lube on the inside of the upper receiver.

cleaning.name: CHARGING HANDLE, BOLT CATCH AND PINS
tasks: Wipe the charging handle and coat its outside with lube.

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Check each magazine is clean and not dented or cracked, the feed lips are not distorted, and the follower moves freely and returns under its own spring.
Do not oil or lubricate magazines or ammunition.

reassembly: Deep clean only: firing pin through its spring and pushed into the carrier until its flange passes the retaining-pin hole; retaining pin back in.
Deep clean only: stock adjustment lever pulled straight down, stock slid over the buffer tube, lever released.
Buffer spring and buffer back into the buffer tube past the buffer retainer — the reverse of their removal; LWRCI's reassembly list does not print this step.
Charging handle in: tabs at its front slid up through the relief cut in the upper, then pushed forward until it latches.
Carrier slid into the upper until it meets the barrel.
Front pivot pin holes lined up and the front pin pushed in until its detent clicks.
Receivers closed together and the rear takedown pin pushed in.
Run the function check before loading.
fncheck: Clear the carbine first. Seat an empty magazine and tug it to be sure the catch holds it. Pull the charging handle back: the carrier must lock to the rear on the empty magazine and the handle must not come forward on its own — push it home until it latches. Drop the magazine; the carrier stays back. Press the large upper paddle of either bolt release: the carrier slams forward into battery (never onto a chamber flag). On SAFE, pull the trigger — the hammer must not fall. On SEMI, pull it — the hammer drops with a loud click. Charge it again holding the trigger down, then release the trigger slowly: you should hear the disconnector click and the hammer must stay cocked. Then clear the carbine again.
